title: Concave Functions and Filtration Subgroups
body_html:
Concave Functions and Filtration Subgroups

Concave functions on the affine root system are the combinatorial input that parametrises the family of compact open subgroups appearing in Bruhat-Tits theory. Parahoric subgroups, Moy-Prasad filtration subgroups, and the Iwahori subgroup all arise as filtration subgroups associated to suitable concave functions.

Setup

Let \(G\) be a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field \(F\). Fix a maximal \(F\)-split torus \(S\), giving the relative root system \(\Phi = \Phi(G, S)\) and the affine root system \(\Psi = \Phi_{\mathrm{aff}}\) (the set of affine functionals \(\alpha + k\) for \(\alpha \in \Phi\), \(k \in \mathbb{R}\)).

Each root subgroup \(U_\alpha(F)\) carries a filtration by the valued root datum: \[ U_{\alpha, r} \;:=\; \{u \in U_\alpha(F) : \varphi_\alpha(u) \ge r\}, \quad r \in \mathbb{R}, \] where \(\varphi_\alpha\) is the valuation on \(U_\alpha(F)\) given by the valued root datum.

Definition

A function \(f : \Phi \to \mathbb{R}\) is concave if for every pair of roots \(\alpha, \beta \in \Phi\) and positive integers \(i, j > 0\) with \(i\alpha + j\beta \in \Phi\): \[ f(i\alpha + j\beta) \;\le\; i\, f(\alpha) + j\, f(\beta). \]

Given a concave function \(f\), the associated filtration subgroup is the subgroup of \(G(F)\) generated by: \[ U_f \;:=\; \bigl\langle T(F)_0, \; U_{\alpha, f(\alpha)} : \alpha \in \Phi \bigr\rangle, \] where \(T(F)_0 \subseteq T(F)\) is the maximal bounded subgroup of the minimal Levi subgroup.

Properties of filtration subgroups

Proposition (Kaletha-Prasad §7.3). For a concave function \(f : \Phi \to \mathbb{R}\):

  1. \(U_f\) is a compact open subgroup of \(G(F)\).
  2. \(U_f\) does not depend on the order of factors in the definition (it is automatically a group due to the concavity condition and the commutator formulas).
  3. The Bruhat-Tits decomposition: \(G(F) = \bigsqcup_{w \in W_{\mathrm{aff}}} U_f \cdot w \cdot U_f\) (a Bruhat decomposition relative to \(U_f\)).
  4. For \(f \le g\) (pointwise): \(U_f \supseteq U_g\), giving a decreasing filtration.

Main examples

Parahoric subgroups. For a point \(x = (x_\alpha)_{\alpha \in \Phi} \in \mathcal{A}(S, F)\) (a point in the apartment, identified with a point in \(V = X_*(S) \otimes_\mathbb{Z} \mathbb{R}\)), the function \[ f_{x,0} : \alpha \mapsto -\alpha(x) \] (evaluation of the linear part of the affine root \(\psi = \alpha + k\) at \(-x\)) is concave, and \(U_{f_{x,0}}\) is the parahoric subgroup \(\mathcal{P}_x^0 = G(F)_{x,0}\).

Moy-Prasad filtration. More generally, for \(r \ge 0\) the function \[ f_{x,r} : \alpha \mapsto -\alpha(x) + r \] is concave, and \(U_{f_{x,r}} = G(F)_{x,r}\) is the \(r\)-th Moy-Prasad filtration subgroup.

Iwahori subgroup. For an alcove \(\mathbf{a}\) with vertex at the origin and \(x\) a point in its interior, the Iwahori subgroup \(I = G(F)_{x,0}\) is the filtration subgroup for \(f = f_{x,0}\). As \(x\) moves within an open alcove, \(G(F)_{x,0}\) is constant and equals the Iwahori subgroup.

Integral models. Each concave function \(f\) gives rise to a smooth affine \(\mathcal{O}_F\)-group scheme \(\mathcal{G}_f\) with \(\mathcal{G}_f(\mathcal{O}_F) = U_f\) (Kaletha-Prasad §8.5 = the concave-function group schemes, generalizing parahorics).

Relation to the Moy-Prasad isomorphism

For \(r > 0\), the successive quotient \[ G(F)_{x,r} \big/ G(F)_{x,r+} \;\cong\; \mathfrak{g}(F)_{x,r} \big/ \mathfrak{g}(F)_{x,r+} \] (the Moy-Prasad isomorphism, K-P §13.5) is an isomorphism of the group-quotient with the corresponding Lie algebra quotient — a finite-dimensional vector space over the residue field.

This Lie algebra quotient decomposes into root spaces: \[ \mathfrak{g}(F)_{x,r} / \mathfrak{g}(F)_{x,r+} \;\cong\; \bigoplus_{\substack{\psi \in \Psi \\ \psi(x) = r}} \mathfrak{g}_\psi / \mathfrak{g}_{\psi+}, \] where the sum is over affine roots \(\psi\) with \(\psi(x) = r\).

Applications

  • Compact induction. The Yu construction of supercuspidal representations uses filtration subgroups \(G_{x,r}\) for a carefully chosen sequence \((x, r)\) to compact-induce representations.
  • Lattice models. Over a \(\mathbb{Z}_p\)-point, the concave function subgroup structure gives a canonical lattice model \(\mathcal{L}_f \subseteq V\) for each algebraic representation \(V\) of \(G\).
  • Integral models of root groups. The filtration subgroups \(U_{\alpha, r}\) of the root groups are the integral models for the filtration subgroups of \(G_a\) — explicit descriptions are in Kaletha-Prasad Appendix C.
